assumptions: Empty and positive droplets form two separable clusters per channel, each well checked by k-means first.
Copies are Poisson-distributed across droplets of the stated volume.
limits: A well whose clusters do not separate is rejected with its reason, not quantified.
Rain between the clusters is assigned by the mixture's cutoff, which moves with the data.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is the template concentration in each ddPCR well, from the raw droplet amplitudes rather than the instrument's count?

description: Two-channel ddPCR droplet-amplitude exports to a template concentration, by CLASSIFYING the raw droplets rather than trusting a count the instrument already made. Four steps in a fixed order, each of which needs the previous one's output: a k-means quality check marks wells whose two droplet clusters are not separable, a plate-wide 1%-slice IQR cutoff marks outlier droplets, a two-component Gaussian mixture per well per channel sets the empty-droplet cutoff on the droplets that survive, and the empty fraction inverts through the Poisson zero term to copies/uL. Reports the cluster the droplets landed in and the reason any well was rejected, so a failed well reads as rejected rather than as a concentration. This is the counterpart of `quantify_dpcr`, not a duplicate: that one starts from per-well positive COUNTS an instrument already classified, this one starts from the amplitudes and does the classifying.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cutoff_iqr.description: how many interquartile ranges above the third quartile of that slice a droplet must sit to be an outlier.

cutoff_sd.description: how many standard deviations above the LOWER mixture component's mean the empty cutoff sits. This is the knob that decides which droplets are empty, and therefore the concentration.

droplet_volume_ul.description: mean volume of ONE droplet, in µL. A per-platform constant: 0.85e-3 µL (0.85 nL) for the Bio-Rad QX200, which is what the QuantaSoft export comes from.

empty_lambda_high.description: largest empty-droplet fraction a well may have. Above it almost every droplet is empty, so there is no positive population to quantify and a concentration would be an extrapolation.

empty_lambda_low.description: smallest empty-droplet fraction a well may have. Below it the smaller k-means cluster is too small to be the empty population, which means the run did not separate.

files.description: the droplet exports, as `<filename>` and its CSV body. QuantaSoft writes one `<name>_<well>_Amplitude.csv` per well with columns `Assay1 Amplitude, Assay2 Amplitude, Cluster`; the well id is read from the FILE NAME because the body does not carry it. Separate files with a line containing only `---`, and start each with `# <filename>`.

random_seed.description: re-seeded before EVERY k-means and EVERY mixture fit, not once per run. Neither has a deterministic start, so this value IS part of the answer: a different seed lands the mixture on a different local optimum and moves the empty cutoff. Upstream's default is 8.

top_percent.description: the top slice of droplets, pooled across the SUCCESSFUL wells, that the outlier cutoff is computed on. One cutoff per axis for the whole plate, not one per well.

total_drops_t.description: fewer accepted droplets than this and the well is rejected before it is clustered at all.

x_var.description: name for the X channel, which is the file's SECOND amplitude column. Bio-Rad's Ch2 is usually HEX or VIC.

y_var.description: name for the Y channel, which is the file's FIRST amplitude column. Bio-Rad's Ch1 is usually FAM.

name: gate_droplets

outlierCutoff.description: the two plate-wide outlier cutoffs, echoed because they were computed from the successful wells only and so depend on which wells passed

params.description: every parameter the run used, including the ones left at their defaults: the seed and the two cutoff multipliers change the concentration, so a reading without them is not comparable

rejected.description: how many wells were rejected by the quality check and so carry no concentration

totalDroplets.description: every droplet read, across every well — the denominator the cluster counts account for

verdicts.description: why each well passed or was rejected, with the k-means the verdict was taken from: both cluster centres, their sizes, their distances to the origin and the gap between them

wells.description: one row per well: droplet counts by cluster, the empty fraction, the per-well cutoffs, and the concentration in copies/uL — null for a rejected well, never a number
